{{Short description|Open online calculus course}}
'''Ximera''' (pronounced “[[chimera]]”) is an open-source, interactive textbook platform, most commonly used in teaching math.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|title = Open Textbook Pilot Grantees Share Vision for Innovative Projects Across the U.S.|url = https://sparcopen.org/news/2023/open-textbook-pilot-grantees-share-vision-for-innovative-projects-across-the-u-s/|website = Scholarly Publishing and Academic Resources Coalition|date = 29 November 2013|access-date = 2025-01-18}}</ref> The name stands for "Ximera: Interactive, Mathematics, Education, Resources, for All."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=The Ximera Project |title=User Manual |url=https://go.osu.edu/xman |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=ximera.osu.edu |language=en}}</ref> Content is authored using [[LaTeX]],<ref name="auto1">{{cite web | url=https://ximera.org/workshops/ | title=Ximera Workshop 2025 }}</ref> and can run on GitHub and Overleaf with no prior installation.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Ximera for accessibility|url=http://go.osu.edu/ximeraforaccess}}</ref><ref name=":0" />  Currently, there are at least 13 courses hosted on Ximera, and it is used by over 45,000 students with an estimated savings of $5.4 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Project |first=Ximera |title=Content |url=https://ximera.org/content/ |access-date=2025-06-06 |website=Ximera Foundation |language=en}}</ref>  A preprint on arXiv was also created with "the help of Ximera".<ref>{{Cite arXiv | last1=Kuan | first1=Jeffrey | title=Introduction to Quantum Groups and Yang-Baxter Equation For Probabilists | date=2025 | class=math.PR | eprint=2512.05782 }}</ref>

== Features ==

Ximera supports embedding of GeoGebra and Desmos interactives with a LaTeX command. An interactive ''answer box'' gives immediate feedback to students, and the grades can be integrated with [[Instructure|Canvas]], the learning management system.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://ximera.osu.edu/xman/ximeraUserManual/gettingWorkDone/desmosAndGeogebra | title=Ximera Manual}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Ximera workshop|url = https://ximera.org/workshops/}}</ref> The accessibility features have also been promoted by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWsxKCoS0RA | title=Webinar by the MAA| website=[[YouTube]]| date=18 December 2024}}</ref>

== Development ==
[[File:Massive Online Open calculus Logo(Calculus One Logo).jpg|thumb|MOOCulus Logo]]The first Ximera course was initially released on [[Coursera]] in the Spring Semester of 2012–13 under the name Calculus One.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Calculus One – ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 cat – Jim Fowler|url = http://kisonecat.com/teaching/2013/calculus-one/|website = kisonecat.com|access-date = 2015-05-19|first = Jim|last = Fowler|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150520133621/http://kisonecat.com/teaching/2013/calculus-one/|archive-date = 2015-05-20|url-status = dead}}</ref> '''MOOCulus''', an online platform that lets you practice Calculus was developed at the Ohio State University to provide students a place to practice Calculus problems. The platform, which was built using [[Ruby on Rails]] was built because Coursera didn't offer an engaging way to practice problems.<ref>{{Cite web|title = MOOCulus for Calculus Fun: An Interview with Tom Evans|url = http://etcjournal.com/2013/07/11/mooculus-for-calculus-fun-an-interview-with-tom-evans/|website = Educational Technology and Change Journal|date = 12 July 2013|access-date = 2015-05-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = What I learned from MOOCulus|url = https://sloopie72.wordpress.com/2013/04/19/what-i-learned-from-mooculus/|website = A Just Recompense|access-date = 2015-05-19|first = Karen|last = Carlson|date = 19 April 2013}}</ref> The whole course, which consists of 200+ videos, was typeset as a [[textbook]] on April 10, 2014. The textbook, which is licensed under ''Creative Commons Attribution Non-commercial Share Alike License,'' incorporated some of its example and exercise problems from [[Elementary calculus: An approach using infinitesimals|Elementary calculus: An approach using Infinitesimals]].<ref>{{Cite book|title = MOOCulus Calculus|pages = 2|url = https://mooculus.osu.edu/textbook/mooculus.pdf|archive-date = 2015-05-19|access-date = 2015-05-19|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150519101156/https://mooculus.osu.edu/textbook/mooculus.pdf|url-status = dead}}</ref>

In 2023, Ximera received a $2.1 million grant from the Department of Education. Students are expected to save $4 million to $10 a year.<ref name="auto"/> As part of the funding, accessibility (defined by [[Web Content Accessibility Guidelines]] 2.1AA) is a requirement, and they partnered with "Tailor Swift Bot" for that work.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ximera.org/partners/ | title=Partners | access-date=2025-04-22 | archive-date=2025-05-25 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525044742/https://ximera.org/partners/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>
This is to comply with [[United States Department of Justice]] rules for Title II of the [[Americans with Disabilities Act]], effective April 2026.<ref name="auto1"/>
